questions.question: Which among the following metals is the best conductor of heat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silver**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Silver is a chemical element with an atomic number 47.
 
• Silver is the best conductor of electricity.
 
• Gold and silver can be separated by the cyanide process.
 
• Siver can be produced as a byproduct of **copper, gold, lead, and zinc refining.**
 
• Silver exhibits the highest electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity among metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One such chemical element is **sodium**.

 
 
• It is an **efficient heat and electricity conductor. **
 
 
 
• **Iron** is atomic number **26** and has the symbol **Fe.**
 
 
• Iron has a** thermal conductivity of 73** at ambient temperature.
 
 
 
• **Gold's** atomic number is **79** and its symbol is **Au.**
 
 
• Compared to silver, gold is more **heat resistant **and has a **higher melting point**.

questions.question: When a household’s income falls below the amount required to sustain basic living standards (food, shelter, housing), is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Absolute Poverty.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Absolute Poverty** refers to the **lack of basic necessities** required to sustain **human life**, such as **food, shelter, and clothing.**
 
• It is a condition of **severe deprivation **of basic human needs, where individuals cannot afford to meet their basic requirements.
 
• Numerous **social, economic, and political** factors can contribute to or result from poverty.

 We are able to enhance the **general health** of every person on the earth by eliminating poverty worldwide. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relative Poverty** refers to the situation where a** person's income falls below** a certain percentage of the median income of the society they live in.
 
• **Generational Poverty** is a situation where **poverty is passed down** from **one generation to the next **due to lack of education, skills, and opportunities.
 
• **Situational Poverty** is a temporary condition where individuals or households **experience poverty due to unforeseen circumstances** such as job loss, illness, or natural disasters.

questions.question: Mention one limitation of the operation of the supermarket.

options.text: A large amount of capital is required to start and run a supermarket.
A customer can get goods of different brands at one place.
They handle a wide range of goods.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a large amount of capital is required to start and run a super market.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Super markets **require a **large amount of capital **to start and run their operations. 
 
• This is due to the high costs involved in **leasing or purchasing** a large retail space, stocking inventory, and hiring employees. 
 
• Additionally, super markets need to invest in **marketing and advertising** to attract customers and stay competitive in the market. 
 
• However, once established, super markets can generate **significant revenue and profits** due to their wide range of products and convenience for customers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Super markets are** large retail stores** that offer a wide range of products to customers under one roof.
 
• These products can range from **groceries, household items, electronics, clothing, **and more.
 
• Super markets are known for their convenience, as customers can **find everything** they need in one place.
 
• They also offer **competitive pricing and promotions** to attract customers and increase sales.

questions.question: Who was the mascot for the 2020 National Games of India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Rubigula **is a **bird species** native to the **Western Ghats**, which is a **mountain range** in India and a biodiversity hotspot.
 
• The choice of Rubigula as the mascot reflects the importance of **preserving India's rich natural heritage.**
 
• The Flame-Throated Bulbul is known for its** distinctive red throat,** which symbolizes the **spirit of the games** and the **passion of the athletes.**
 
• The choice of Rubigula as the mascot also highlights the** need for conservation efforts** to protect endangered species like this bird.

questions.question: Mahamastakabhisheka is a Jain festival celebrated once in every ______ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahamastak Abhishek** is a **grand Jain festival** celebrated once in every **12 years.**
 
• It is celebrated to anoint the statue of **Bahubali.**
 
• The festival is celebrated with great **enthusiasm and devotion** by Jains all over the world.
 
• The festival is celebrated in the city of **Shravanabelagola,** located in the **Hassan district** of **Karnataka,** India.
 
• Mahamastak Abhishek is a significant event for Jains as it is believed to bring **blessings and good fortune** to the participants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The purpose of the festival is to **honor a 17.4-meter-tall monolithic monument** of Siddha Bahubali.
 
• The next ceremony for the anointing is scheduled for **2030**; the last one happened in **February of 2018.**
 
• The 2018 ritual was the second Mahamastakabhisheka of the twenty-first century and is believed to be the **88th in a series **that started in **981 AD. **
 
• **Many Jain ascetics** are scheduled to grace the ritual.
 
• From February 17 to 25, 2018, the event in Shravanabelagola, India, was led by **Charukeerthi Bhattaraka Swamiji. **

questions.question: Aim of last (twelfth) five year plan was:

options.text: Faster, Sustainable, and More Inclusive Growth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Faster, Sustainable, and More Inclusive Growth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The aim of the **twelfth five year plan **was **Faster, Sustainable, and More Inclusive Growth.**
 
• Faster growth refers to the aim of **increasing the GDP growth rate** of the country.
 
• Sustainable growth refers to the aim of ensuring that economic growth is not at the cost of **environmental degradation** and** depletion of natural resources.**
 
• More Inclusive Growth refers to the aim of ensuring that the benefits of economic growth are distributed **more equally** among different sections of the society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Twelveth Five-Year Plan** (2012–17) aims for an** eight percent** yearly growth rate. 
 
• **10% poverty reduction** is the government's target for the 12th Five-Year Plan, and this objective has mainly been met because to the government's initiatives to combat poverty.
 
• India's **policies, programs, and projects** are given a broad direction and a foundational structure by the Five Year Plans (FYPs).

questions.question: Which one of the following is the oldest football competition in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Durand Cup.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **oldest football competition** in India is the **Durand Cup.**
 
• It was first held in **1888,** making it the** third oldest** football tournament in the world.
 
• It is named after **Sir Mortimer Durand**, who was the** Foreign Secretary** in British India.
 
• The tournament was initially meant for **British Indian Army teams**, but civilian teams were allowed to participate from **1940 onwards.**
 
• The Durand Cup has been won by top Indian clubs like **Mohun Bagan, East Bengal, and Salgaocar.**
 
• The tournament was **not held in 2020 **due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BC Roy Trophy:**

 
 
• This is a football tournament for **under-19 teams** from different Indian states.
 
• It was first held in** 1960** and is named after **Bidhan Chandra Roy**, who was the** second Chief Minister of West Bengal.**
 
• The tournament has helped in the discovery of **young football talent** in India.
 
 
 
• **Santosh Trophy:**
 
 
• This is a football tournament for **state teams** in India.
 
• It was first held in **1941** and is named after the **Maharaja of Santosh,** who donated the trophy.
 
• The tournament has been won by many different** state teams** over the years.
 
 
 
• **Federation Cup:**
 
 
• This was a football tournament for **club teams** in India.
 
• It was first held in **1977** and was last held in **2017.**
 
• The tournament was replaced by the **Super Cup**, which was also discontinued in** 2019.**

questions.question: Who breaks down waste into smaller particles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**detritivores.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Detritivores** are the organisms that **break down waste** into **smaller particles.**
 
• They are also known as **decomposers**, and they break down dead organic matter into simpler compounds.
 
• Detritivores play a crucial role in **nutrient cycling, **as they release the nutrients back into the ecosystem for the use of other organisms.
 
• Examples of detritivores include **earthworms, dung beetles, snails**, and some species of** bacteria and fungi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnivores **are organisms that **feed** on other animals.

 
 
• Carnivores are sometimes referred to as **predators. **
 
• **Prey** is the term for the organisms that carnivores hunt.
 
 
 
• **Omnivores **are organisms that consume both **plants and animals**.
 
 
• Omnivores **metabolize the nutrients** and energy from the sources they consume in addition to digesting fiber, protein, fat, and carbs.
 
 
 
• **Herbivores **are organisms that feed on **plants**.
 
 
• The sizes of herbivores vary, ranging from** little insects** like aphids to massive, **hulking elephants.**

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution does a citizen have the freedom to practice any profession or occupation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 19 (1) (g).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 19 (1) (g)** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to practice any** profession, occupation, trade or business.**
 
• This right can be **restricted by the State** for reasons such as **public interest, morality, and health.**
 
• The freedom to practice any profession or occupation is an essential aspect of the **right to livelihood, **which is a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution.
 
• This right is crucial for individuals to pursue their chosen **career paths** and contribute to the** economic growth** of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 22 (b)** guarantees** protection against arrest and detention **in certain cases.
 
• **Article 21 (A) **guarantees the **right to education.**
 
• **Article 20 (c)** guarantees protection against **self-incrimination.**

questions.question: Who among the following met the Buddha to get his advice on the proposed attack on Vajjis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vassakara**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vassakara** was the **chief of the Licchavis** who approached the **Buddha** to seek his advice on the proposed **attack on Vajjis.**
 
• The Buddha advised him **against the attack** and gave him a **discourse** on the virtues of a good ruler and the importance of maintaining **social harmony.**
 
• **Yashas** was a youth who became a disciple of the **Buddha**.
 
 
• He is known for his devotion and his contribution to **spreading the teachings** of the Buddha.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka **was a **Mauryan emperor **who converted to Buddhism after witnessing the horrors of war.
 
 
• He is known for his efforts to spread the teachings of the Buddha and for his policies of **non-violence.**
 
 
 
• **Radhagupta **was a trusted minister of Emperor Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Vajjis** were a **confederacy of eight clans** in ancient India.

 
 
• They were known for their **democratic system of government** and for their **military prowess.**
 
 
 
• The **Buddha **was a **spiritual teacher** who lived in ancient India.
 
 
• He is the **founder of Buddhism **and is revered as a great teacher and a wise philosopher.
 
 
 
• The **Licchavis** were a clan of the Vajjis who were known for their **bravery and their military strength.**
 
 
• They were also known for their close relationship with the Buddha and for their patronage of the** Buddhist teachings.**

questions.question: Which among the following dance forms is a unique dance form as the performers are dressed as women and is popular in the parts of Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gotipua.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gotipua** is a unique dance form from the state of **Odisha** where **young boys** are dressed up as** women** and perform **acrobatic dance moves. **
 
• It was traditionally performed in **temples** and was a way of offering devotion to **Lord Jagannath.**
 
• Gotipua literally means** "single boy"** and the performers are usually between the ages of** 6 to 14 years old.**
 
• The dance form was popularized in the **16th century **by the poet and saint **Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fugdi** is a folk dance form from the western Indian state of** Goa** and is performed by women during weddings and other celebrations.

 
 
• Fugdi is usually performed by** women in a circle formation** and is accompanied by traditional Goan music.
 
 
 
• **Theyyam** is a popular **ritualistic dance** form from the northern parts of **Kerala.**
 
 
• It is performed by **men** dressed up in elaborate costumes.
 
 
 
• **Bihu** is a folk dance form from the state of **Assam **and is performed during the **Bihu festival.**
 
 
• **​**It is performed by both** men and women** and is characterized by **energetic dance moves.**
 
• Bihu is a celebration of the** harvest season** and is performed with traditional musical instruments like the **dhol, pepa and gogona.**

questions.question: The climate of India is described as the ______ type.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**monsoon.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **climate of India **is mainly influenced by the **monsoon winds,** which bring **heavy rainfall** in the **summer season.**
 
• The monsoon climate is characterized by a **distinct wet and dry season,** with **high humidity and temperature** during the summer months and cool and dry weather during the winter months.
 
• The monsoon type of climate is found in many parts of South Asia, including **India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Nepal.**
 
• The monsoon climate is crucial for the **agriculture and economy** of India, as it provides water for irrigation and supports the growth of crops like **rice, wheat, and sugarcane.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India** is home to **six primary climatic subtypes**, based on the **Köppen system.**
 
• These subtypes include alpine tundra and glaciers in the** north, **wet tropical regions that support rain forests in the **southwest**, and island territories. Arid deserts are found in the **west. **
 
• With certain local modifications, the **meteorological department** of the nation observes the** four seasons** as defined by the international community: **winter** (December to February), **summer **(March to May), **monsoon** (June to September), and a **post-monsoon period** (October and November).
 
• Midway through India is where the **Tropic of Cancer** is located.

questions.question: Major aspect of Green revolution is that, it has made India ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Self-Sufficient.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Green revolution** refers to a series of **agricultural practices and technologies** introduced in India in the **1960s and 1970s** to increase agricultural productivity and combat **food shortages.**
 
• One of the major objectives of the green revolution was to make India** self-sufficient **in food production.
 
• The country had been heavily dependent on** food imports **before the green revolution.
 
• The green revolution brought about significant improvements in **crop yields**, especially for **wheat and rice**, which are staple food crops in India.
 
• This helped to increase food production and reduce the** country's dependence** on food imports.
 
• The green revolution also led to the adoption of **new technologies **like high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides, which further boosted agricultural productivity.
 
• Today, India is one of the** largest food producers** in the world, and the green revolution is widely credited with transforming the country from a food-deficit nation to a food-surplus nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The country's major** agricultural exports** include** rice, wheat, spices, tea, and cotton.**
 
• India is the **largest exporter of rice** in the world, accounting for around** 30% **of global rice exports.
 
• It is also a **major exporter of wheat**, with exports accounting for around** 10% of global wheat trade.**
 
• The green revolution helped to **reduce** the country's dependence on **food imports**, and today India is largely self-sufficient in food production.
 
• While India is a major producer of **cash crops** like cotton, sugarcane, and tobacco, these crops are** not** the main focus of the green revolution.
 
• The green revolution primarily aimed to increase the productivity of staple food crops like** wheat and rice, **which are crucial for food security in India.
